owner_instruction.context: claude-fable-5, the model pinned by the 2026-07-23 Claude-gate amendment, is quota-exhausted account-wide until 2026-08-04, with the canary halted at 554/945 cells

deviation: this IS the deviation the frozen amendment names by title: 'Reviewer model/build change mid-canary is a protocol deviation.' It is taken knowingly, on the owner's instruction, and disclosed here rather than absorbed silently.

reviewer.effort_rationale: reasoning effort is a model-VISIBLE generation setting and is bound here for the same reason the frozen roster pins reasoning_effort for openai/gpt-oss-120b
reviewer.transport: codex CLI 0.145.0 `codex exec`, authenticated via the owner's ChatGPT subscription (not API billing); one fresh ephemeral session per payload in an empty working root, with --ignore-user-config and --ignore-rules so no project context is loaded
reviewer.prompt_delivery: the hash-verified packet file is piped as stdin, so the model receives exactly the bytes on disk; their sha256 is recorded per ruling and checked at commit time against the frozen subagent_prompt_sha256

controls_preserved: prompt integrity: 80/80 rulings carry a prompt hash equal to the frozen packet hash
blindness: 80/80 event streams contained zero command_execution items
parseability: 80/80 parsed as the frozen three-line format; zero malformed
failures would have committed as reviewer_error (non-ALLOW); none occurred
disclosed_weaknesses: codex's read-only sandbox restricts WRITES, not reads: a probe confirmed the reviewer process CAN read the world documents from disk. Blindness is therefore enforced by detection and refusal (any ruling whose event stream shows a command is discarded), not by prevention. No ruling in this batch triggered it, but the guarantee is empirical rather than structural.

the substitute reviewer shares a model family with the external Codex consults that adjudicated this protocol (#23-#28), so the adjudicator is no longer fully independent of the gate operator; flagged for the adjudicator to weigh

observed_clause_distributions.note: CONFOUNDED: the two reviewers ruled DISJOINT payload sets (fable slot-1, substitute mostly slot-2), so these differences mix reviewer identity with payload composition and must not be read as a pure inter-reviewer effect
observed_clause_distributions.salient_pattern: near-identical ALLOW rate (66% vs 61%) but close to inverted reject attribution: fable cites P3 compound for 74% of its rejects, the substitute cites P2 restatement for 68% of its rejects
observed_clause_distributions.how_to_disentangle: re-review a sample of already-fable-ruled payloads with the substitute (or the reverse once quota returns) to obtain a paired comparison on identical inputs; not yet done

Canary results estimate the system with a HETEROGENEOUS gate: 141 payloads ruled by claude-fable-5 and 80 by gpt-5.6-sol.
